messages.subject: I: spatial distance sampling
parts:
Hello,

with reference to my previous question dated 29/11/04 I was able to =
write a software to apply a methods described in chapter 4 (section 4.3) =
of the book Advanced distance sampling by Buckland et al.

and that system seems working appropriately in the sense that the model =
predicts the distribution of radiocollared fallow deer in the area.

However some doubts remain.

1. I've used 4 surveys to estimate local fallow deer density. To do that =
I used the ESW estimated by pooling the data of the 4 surveys and the =
waiting distance I used all points of the 4 surveys. By instance=20

A------B-----A------------C (translated transect of fig 4.1)
x1.....x2...x3...........x4 coordinates

I computed l_i=3Dx2-x1 between A and B, between B and A (x3-x2) and so =
on where A,B,C are detection points from the first, second,.. survey.

I argued that the density obtained is the "average density" of the 4 =
surveys but I worry whether or I've to divide by 4 (or for some other =
value) to obtain it?

2. Fallow deer occurs in clusters. For each point of the grid used to =
extrapolate the model, I used the following equations derived by eq. =
(4.1)

D_hat=3Ds_hat/2*mu_hat*l_hat

where s_hat is the average cluster size per habitat (we detected no size =
bias). Is this correct or there are smarter way to modelise s_hat?

thanks,

Stefano

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: I: spatial distance sampling
parts:
> > with reference to my previous question dated 29/11/04 I was able to write a software to apply a methods described in chapter 4 (section 4.3) of the book Advanced distance sampling by Buckland et al.
> >
> > and that system seems working appropriately in the sense that the model predicts the distribution of radiocollared fallow deer in the area.
> >
> > However some doubts remain.
> >
> > 1. I've used 4 surveys to estimate local fallow deer density. To do that I used the ESW estimated by pooling the data of the 4 surveys and the waiting distance I used all points of the 4 surveys. By instance

> >
> > A------B-----A------------C (translated transect of fig 4.1)
> > x1.....x2...x3...........x4 coordinates
> >

> > I computed l_i=x2-x1 between A and B, between B and A (x3-x2) and so on where A,B,C are detection points from the first, second,.. survey.
> >
> > I argued that the density obtained is the "average density" of the 4 surveys but I worry whether or I've to divide by 4 (or for some other value) to obtain it?

Yes, by pooling, you're increased the encounter rate fourfold, so you will
need to divide the density estimate by 4.

> > 2. Fallow deer occurs in clusters. For each point of the grid used to extrapolate the model, I used the following equations derived by eq. (4.1)
> >
> > D_hat=s_hat/2*mu_hat*l_hat
> >
> > where s_hat is the average cluster size per habitat (we detected no size bias). Is this correct or there are smarter way to modelise s_hat?

That should be fine. You could also fit a spatial model for s - see p68
of the advanced distance sampling book.

Steve Buckland
